name: HALO
summary: A low-maintenance supernova neutrino detector at SNOLAB uses recycled lead and SNO helium-3 counters to detect a sudden burst of neutrons.
detection_principle: Charged-current and neutral-current neutrino interactions excite lead nuclei, which may emit one or two neutrons. Moderated neutrons are captured in helium-3 proportional counters; the detector records neutron multiplicity rather than Cherenkov rings.

status.label: Operating / data taking
status.evidence: SNOLAB labels HALO Running and the 2025 collaboration talk documents thirteen years of operation.

timeline.event: First acquisition from the full set of proportional counters.
Collaboration reported thirteen years of operation.

results.summary: Long-lived operation and low-latency neutron-burst alarms were reported. HALO-1kT is a separate future enlargement concept, not the installed detector mass.
